title.narrative: Activity under preparation Sustainable Value Chains in Food Systems

description.narrative: Current food systems ¿ encompassing agricultural, aquatic, and livestock production ¿ are environmentally unsustainable, contributing significantly to biodiversity loss, ecosystem degradation and desertification, climate change, pollution, and deforestation. They are also structurally fragile and, therefore, cannot be relied upon to feed the world over the long term especially in a context where food security has become increasingly geopolitical. Moreover, they drive global trends toward poor diets and diet-related diseases, while failing to provide adequate opportunities for decent livelihoods, particularly for young people, women, and persons with disabilities.The proposed Action seeks to foster the transformation of agrifood systems into ones that are economically viable, socially equitable, environmentally sustainable and climate resilient. This will be achieved through the development of efficient value chains embedded in robust governance structures and mechanisms at national and territorial levels, across three complementary components. Component 1 (EUR 11.00 million) supports investments in sustainable, resilient, inclusive, and efficient agricultural and food value chains, in full alignment with the Global Gateway strategy. This will be pursued through two sub-components:Sub-component 1.1 (second phase of the AGRINFO Project) monitors, analyses, and translates new or increasingly stringent EU sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) regulations into accessible, timely, and actionable guidance for producers, exporters, competent authorities, and policymakers in partner countries seeking to maintain or improve access to the EU market.Sub-component 1.2 (second phase of the SATAF Project) strengthens linkages between local agricultural producers and international market actors, especially European buyers, financial institutions, and research organisations, in selected value chains based on agroecology and agroforestry, for both export and domestic markets.Component 2 (EUR 5.45 million) strengthens multistakeholder governance and land tenure legal frameworks to enable responsible, inclusive investment in agrifood systems, through two sub-components:Sub-component 2.1 supports the Committee on World Food Security (CFS) Secretariat and its civil society and private sector mechanisms to function effectively as a space for active multilateralism and open dialogue toward sustainable agrifood systems transformation.Sub-component 2.2 enhances the sustainability, technical soundness, and social legitimacy of agrifood investments through a coherent, on-demand support mechanism covering land governance, community engagement, and capacity-building for policy implementation.Component 3 (EUR 11.00 million) aims to catalyse the impact of research on agricultural innovation and its scaling across agrifood systems, through continued support to CGIAR Centres as part of the EU pledge of EUR 140 million (September 2021).
